messages:
Sam: Heads-up — spotted a spike of 429s from the edge into us-west starting ~18:12 UTC. p95 gen latency jumped from 220ms -> 1.9s for affected traffic. Root cause unclear, opening thread to capture handoff notes.
IncidentBot: Pager triggered: "EDGE->ORIGIN TLS handshake failures (us-west)" — 76 alerts in last 5m. Severity: P2. Pager link: https://incident.redwood/INC-8342
Alex: I'm primary on this shift, taking lead. Confirming: are the 429s manifesting as 429 on our routers or upstream?
Maya: I'm secondary and available. I see 429s from router logs with upstream peer error code `ECONNRESET` + TLS handshake errors in the socktrace. A subset of requests show `TLS alert 40` in edge logs.
Ron: Observed a correlated jump in origin connection pool usage + a surge of TLS handshake timeouts. Grafana dashboards: https://grafana.redwood/d/edge/egress?orgId=1
Alex: Quick mitigation plan: 1) enable ingress fallback to eu-west for non-SLA traffic 2) increase origin connection pool on routers from 120 -> 200 3) temporarily mark low-priority customers as best-effort so we don't exhaust pools for critical customers.
Sam: +1 on priorities. Can someone run the fallback toggle? I can do the pool bump if ops approves.
Ron: I'll open a change: `router:increase-connpool-1765439999` and apply to canary (2 nodes) then roll. Command: ```./ctl router set conn_pool_size=200 --canary 2```
DeployBot: Change queued: router:increase-connpool-1765439999 — will start canary deploy in 2m. CI checks passed.
Alex: FYI, I'm enabling eu-west fallback for non-critical routes now. Steps in runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/egress-fallback — following the checklist.
Maya: After fallback flip, error rate dropped ~60% in 10m for the affected cohort. p95 back to ~350ms. Still seeing a constant trickle of handshake errors for a small subset (~4% of requests).
IncidentBot: Note: Customer-impact tag added: `partial_degradation: low-to-medium` — approx 5 customers experienced repeated 429/timeout windows. Customer IDs sampled: C-1291, C-8414, C-0992.
Alex: Logged workaround: added temporary rate-limit-bypass for C-1291/C-8414 while we investigate. Applied via quota service: `quota:grant C-1291 bypass=true ttl=6h`.
Ron: Can we capture a tcpdump of the failing origin connections? If this is a TLS handshake edge case we need packet-level. I'll spin up capture on router-node-14. Command: `sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -s 0 -w /tmp/tls-fail.pcap host origin-usw-3`
Sam: Good call. Ron, coordinate with infra to get pcap off-node to secure storage. Also ping CDN support (Fastly) — there were reports of partial handshakes earlier this week.
Maya: Logged a ticket with CDN: https://support.fastly/tickets/5567 — included sample pcap and edge logs. Waiting on triage.
Alex: Current status summary for next shift: primary = Alex, secondary = Maya. Mitigations applied: eu-west fallback enabled for non-critical traffic, conn pool increased (canary done, rolling), temporary bypass for high-impact customers. Customer impact: limited to small set, no full outages. Next steps for morning shift: 1) follow up with Fastly support 2) analyze pcap and TLS cipher negotiation failures 3) consider rolling TLS downgrade to allow problematic handshake patterns (last-resort) 4) prepare postmortem if Fastly confirms a service degradation.
Sam: Action items assigned: 
- Alex: follow up with support thread + next-shift briefing (due by 08:30 UTC)
- Maya: run deeper log correlation across edge->origin traces and produce a sample repro list (due EOD)
- Ron: upload pcap and attach to incident ticket (done ASAP)
- OpsEng: monitor metrics and pause rollouts if error rate climbs >15% over baseline

Maya: Minor note — there is a coverage gap between 02:00–06:00 UTC tomorrow (only one oncall in APAC). If this escalates overnight please page the on-call manager (pager policy alpha).
Alex: Acknowledged. I'll coordinate with on-call manager to add an extra rotation if Fastly doesn't confirm next 6h.
IncidentBot: Incident status changed to "Mitigated (partial)". Postmortem required if customer impact confirmed.
Sam: Thanks team — leaving thread in read/write for the night crew. I'll drop a short summary to #general at 19:00 UTC. :thumbsup:
